subtitle: std::<exception> — the foundational exception-handling header. restd's role mirrors <new>: the exception runtime (the base types, the terminate handler slot, the exception_ptr / nested-exception machinery) is provided by the language runtime and the C++ ABI, so restd ships namespace-consistent re-exports (using-declarations) that preserve type identity across the std/restd boundary, plus targeted back-ports where they are genuinely portable. Two back-port wins reach C++98: get_terminate (added to std in C++11) via a set-time shadow slot, and uncaught_exceptions (added in C++17) at boolean precision. The C++11 exception_ptr family (exception_ptr, current_exception, rethrow_exception, make_exception_ptr) and the nested-exception family (nested_exception, throw_with_nested, rethrow_if_nested) are re-exported on C++11+ and have no portable C++98 path. Every C++98-baseline symbol additionally carries a freestanding fallback gated on D_ENV_CPP98_HAS_EXCEPTION so the module never hard-fails. No dependency on <string_view> or on any not-yet-shipped restd::type_traits.
legend_blurb: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <exception> header. Mostly re-export of runtime/ABI-provided symbols, with two back-ports (get_terminate -> C++98, uncaught_exceptions -> C++98 at boolean precision). The C++11 exception_ptr and nested-exception families are runtime/ABI-bound and cannot reach C++98.

symbols.name: exception
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::exception. Type identity preserved — catch(std::exception&) catches restd-thrown exceptions and vice versa; restd modules throw restd::exception-derived types to stay in-namespace. Freestanding fallback (when D_ENV_CPP98_HAS_EXCEPTION is 0): a minimal standalone base with virtual what(); does not participate in catch(std::exception&) since there is no std::exception to relate to.

symbols.name: bad_exception
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::bad_exception (thrown by the runtime when exception handling itself fails). Freestanding fallback derives from restd::exception with what() returning "bad_exception".

symbols.name: terminate / set_terminate / terminate_handler
symbols.notes: Re-exports of std::terminate ([[noreturn]]), std::set_terminate, and the std::terminate_handler typedef (void (*)()). On C++98 set_terminate is a thin wrapper that records the handler in a function-local-static shadow slot (so the get_terminate back-port can read it) before delegating to std::set_terminate; on C++11+ it is a pure using-declaration. Freestanding fallback reimplements the whole facility over the shadow slot, with terminate() invoking the slot then abort().

symbols.name: get_terminate
symbols.notes: C++11+: using-declaration from std::get_terminate. C++98 back-port: returns the handler last installed via restd::set_terminate (function-local-static shadow), the same scheme as <new>'s get_new_handler. Caveat: a direct std::set_terminate call is invisible to the shadow. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: surfaced on C++98, 13-year back-port.

symbols.name: uncaught_exception
symbols.notes: C++98-C++14: using-declaration from std::uncaught_exception. From C++17 onward restd routes through its own shim (uncaught_exceptions() > 0) rather than the deprecated std::uncaught_exception, which avoids -Wdeprecated-declarations at the call site and keeps the spelling alive past its C++20 removal from std (restd backwards-compatibility goal). Deprecated in std in C++17, removed in C++20.

symbols.name: uncaught_exceptions
symbols.notes: C++17+: using-declaration from std::uncaught_exceptions (exact in-flight count). Pre-C++17 back-port: boolean precision only — returns uncaught_exception() ? 1 : 0. The exact count is deliberately NOT recovered pre-C++17: the underlying counter is exposed inconsistently across runtimes (libc++abi ships extern "C" __cxa_uncaught_exceptions; libstdc++ ships only the C++-mangled std::uncaught_exceptions gated behind C++17 headers), and restd will not emit a reference that may fail to link. Correct for "is any exception in flight?"; lossy for nested unwinding depth. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: spelling surfaced on C++98.

symbols.name: exception_ptr
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::exception_ptr (opaque, copyable, null-comparable handle to a captured exception). Re-exported on C++11+ only.
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98 — exception_ptr is an opaque, ABI-provided handle (the Itanium/MS C++ ABI __cxa_* exception machinery). There is no portable way to capture and store an in-flight exception without runtime support, so restd re-exports std rather than reimplementing (the same posture <new> takes toward operator new).

symbols.name: current_exception
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::current_exception. Returns an exception_ptr to the exception currently being handled, or a null exception_ptr outside a handler.
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98 — capture of the in-flight exception is runtime/ABI-provided (same __cxa_* machinery as exception_ptr). Re-exported from std on C++11+.

symbols.name: rethrow_exception
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::rethrow_exception ([[noreturn]]); re-raises the exception referenced by an exception_ptr.
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98 — re-raising a captured exception_ptr is runtime/ABI-provided. Re-exported from std on C++11+.

symbols.name: make_exception_ptr
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::make_exception_ptr (captures a copy of a value as an exception_ptr, effectively try{throw e;}catch(...){return current_exception();}).
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98 — built on current_exception (ABI-provided). Re-exported from std on C++11+.

symbols.name: nested_exception
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::nested_exception (mixin whose ctor captures current_exception(); nested_ptr() / rethrow_nested() are RTTI-backed). Re-exported on C++11+.
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98 — captures current_exception() in its ctor and rethrows via the C++11 exception_ptr facility (ABI/RTTI). Re-exported from std on C++11+.

symbols.name: throw_with_nested
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::throw_with_nested ([[noreturn]]). Re-exporting std's implementation also sidesteps the class/final/base-of trait analysis it performs internally — restd::type_traits does not yet ship is_class / is_base_of / decay, so a reimplementation would be blocked; the re-export is not.
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98 — depends on nested_exception / current_exception (C++11 ABI). Re-exported from std on C++11+ rather than reimplemented.

symbols.name: rethrow_if_nested
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::rethrow_if_nested. Uses a polymorphic dynamic_cast over the nested_exception base internally (RTTI). Re-exported on C++11+.
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98 — depends on nested_exception and a polymorphic dynamic_cast over the C++11 facility. Re-exported from std on C++11+.
